Finds web corpora (Pile-CC), not nominally 'high-quality' data like Wikipedia, have the strongest positive correlation with downstream performance; single-task performance varies by up to 14.6%.

papers.title: Scaling Parameter-Constrained Language Models with Quality Data
papers.abstract: Extends scaling laws with a microscopic view of data quality via an 'effective training tokens' term combining text diversity and syntheticity.
findings: Introduces 'effective training tokens' as a function of text diversity and syntheticity (measured by a teacher model)
Pretrained over 200 models of 25M to 1.5B parameters on sampled synthetic data
Relates text quality, model size, training tokens, and accuracy across eight reasoning tasks, showing quality is critical for parameter-constrained models

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Precision
papers.abstract: Devises precision-aware scaling laws for training and inference, modeling how low-precision training and post-training quantization affect loss and effective parameter count.
findings: Training in lower precision reduces a model's 'effective parameter count', enabling prediction of additional loss from low-precision training
Degradation from post-training quantization increases as models are trained on more data, eventually making additional pretraining data actively harmful
Suggests training larger models in lower precision may be compute-optimal

papers.title: FrontierMath: A Benchmark for Evaluating Advanced Mathematical Reasoning in AI
papers.abstract: A benchmark of hundreds of original, exceptionally difficult unpublished mathematics problems spanning major branches of modern math, with automated verification to minimize contamination risk.
findings: Developed in collaboration with over 60 mathematicians, including IMO question writers and Fields medalists
Problems span computational number theory to abstract algebraic geometry and typically require hours or days for expert mathematicians to solve
Leading AI models solve less than 2% of FrontierMath problems despite near-perfect scores on GSM-8k and MATH

papers.title: Tulu 3: Pushing Frontiers in Open Language Model Post-Training
papers.abstract: A fully open post-training recipe (data, code, weights) over SFT, DPO, and a new Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) stage, popularizing the RLVR term for skills with checkable answers.
findings: Introduces and names RLVR (Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards), training on tasks with checkable answers like math and precise instruction-following.
Tulu 3 (on Llama 3.1 bases) surpasses the instruct versions of Llama 3.1, Qwen 2.5, Mistral and even GPT-4o-mini and Claude 3.5-Haiku on its evaluation suite.
Releases full data, training code, recipes, and a decontaminated multi-task evaluation framework with held-out unseen evals.

edges.note: RLVR gains may be elicitation, not teaching

papers.title: Nemotron-CC: Transforming Common Crawl into a Refined Long-Horizon Pretraining Dataset
papers.abstract: Presents methods for building a high-quality 6.3T-token pretraining dataset from Common Crawl that balances data quantity with accuracy, using classifier ensembling, synthetic data rephrasing, and reduced reliance on heuristic filters to retain far more unique tokens for long-horizon training.
findings: High-quality subset improves MMLU by 5.6 points over DCLM when training 8B models for 1T tokens.
Full 6.3T-token dataset matches DCLM on MMLU while containing four times more unique real tokens.
An 8B model trained for 15T tokens achieves +5 on MMLU versus Llama 3.1 8B.
Same model shows +3.1 on ARC-Challenge versus Llama 3.1 8B, and +0.5 average across ten diverse tasks.
Combines classifier ensembling, synthetic rephrasing, and reduced heuristic filtering to retain more tokens.

papers.title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
papers.abstract: Technical report for DeepSeek-V3, a 671B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model (37B activated per token) using Multi-head Latent Attention and DeepSeekMoE, trained with an auxiliary-loss-free load-balancing strategy and FP8 training at scale.
findings: 671B total parameters with 37B activated per token; uses MLA for efficient inference and fine-grained DeepSeekMoE for cost-effective training.
Pioneers an auxiliary-loss-free load-balancing strategy and a multi-token prediction (MTP) training objective.
Trained on 14.8T tokens using FP8 mixed-precision training, with full training costing about 2.788M H800 GPU-hours.
Introduces DualPipe pipeline parallelism and optimized all-to-all communication to overlap computation and communication in MoE training.
Achieves performance competitive with leading closed models while remaining open-weight and compute-efficient.

papers.title: AutoScale: Scale-Aware Data Mixing for Pre-Training LLMs
papers.abstract: Shows that data mixtures performing well at small scales do not retain their advantage at larger scales, and proposes AutoScale, a two-stage scale-aware data composition framework that fits a parametric loss model at small budgets and extrapolates the optimal composition to larger budgets without further retraining.
findings: Achieves 28% faster perplexity reduction than baselines when pretraining GPT-2 Large.
Delivers up to a 38% speed-up over unweighted training.
Demonstrates that data mixtures optimal at small scales may not retain their advantage at larger scales.
Predicts optimal composition at large budgets via small-budget proxy fits, avoiding costly retraining, and achieves best-average results on downstream tasks.

papers.title: Kimi k1.5: Scaling Reinforcement Learning with LLMs
papers.abstract: Reports the RL training of Kimi k1.5, a multimodal reasoning LLM, emphasizing long-context scaling and a simplified RL framework that avoids MCTS, value functions, and process reward models.
findings: Achieves strong reasoning via long-context RL scaling without Monte Carlo tree search, value functions, or process reward models.
Reports state-of-the-art reasoning performance matching o1-level results on math/code/vision benchmarks (e.g. AIME, MATH-500, Codeforces).
Introduces effective long2short methods that transfer long-CoT reasoning gains into shorter-CoT models.

papers.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Shows reasoning can emerge from pure large-scale RL (DeepSeek-R1-Zero, no SFT cold start) and that a multi-stage cold-start + RL pipeline (DeepSeek-R1) reaches o1-level reasoning, with distilled smaller models released.
findings: DeepSeek-R1-Zero is trained via large-scale RL with no supervised fine-tuning, yet develops emergent self-reflection, verification, and strategy adaptation.
DeepSeek-R1 (multi-stage training with cold-start data before RL) achieves performance comparable to OpenAI-o1-1217 on reasoning tasks.
Open-sources R1-Zero, R1, and six dense distilled models (1.5B, 7B, 8B, 14B, 32B, 70B) based on Qwen and Llama.

papers.title: Humanity's Last Exam
papers.abstract: A multi-modal benchmark of expert-written questions at the frontier of human knowledge, created in response to MMLU-style saturation, with unambiguous, verifiable solutions that resist internet retrieval.
findings: Consists of 2,500 questions across dozens of subjects developed globally by subject-matter experts
Motivated by saturation: LLMs now exceed 90% accuracy on benchmarks like MMLU
State-of-the-art LLMs show low accuracy and poor calibration, with RMS calibration errors above 70% across all models

papers.title: MedXpertQA: Benchmarking Expert-Level Medical Reasoning and Understanding
papers.abstract: A challenging benchmark for expert-level medical knowledge and reasoning with both text and multimodal components, built through rigorous filtering, augmentation, and expert review, and including a reasoning-focused subset for advanced models.
findings: Contains 4,460 questions spanning 17 medical specialties and 11 body systems.
Includes Text and MM (multimodal) subsets; the MM subset uses expert-level exam questions with diverse images and rich clinical information.
Evaluates 18 leading models.
Designed to go beyond image-caption QA pairs of standard medical benchmarks, stressing multi-step clinical reasoning.

papers.title: s1: Simple Test-Time Scaling
papers.abstract: Demonstrates simple test-time scaling via a tiny curated SFT dataset plus 'budget forcing' to control inference-time compute, achieving strong reasoning with minimal data.
findings: Curates s1K, just 1,000 questions with reasoning traces selected for difficulty, diversity, and quality.
Introduces budget forcing: forcibly terminate thinking or extend it by appending 'Wait' to lengthen reasoning at test time.
After SFT on s1K, Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct (s1) exceeds o1-preview on competition math (MATH and AIME24) by up to 27%.
Budget forcing enables test-time scaling where extending thinking improves accuracy on AIME24.
Model, data, and code are fully open-sourced, showing strong reasoning is achievable with extremely small SFT data.

papers.title: SmolLM2: When Smol Goes Big -- Data-Centric Training of a Small Language Model
papers.abstract: Describes the data-centric training of SmolLM2, a 1.7B-parameter language model trained on ~11 trillion tokens through a multi-stage process that mixes web data with specialized datasets, introducing new curated datasets (FineMath, Stack-Edu, SmolTalk) to fill gaps in existing resources.
findings: SmolLM2 is a 1.7B-parameter model trained on approximately 11 trillion tokens.
Uses multi-stage training that interleaves web data with specialized datasets, refining mixtures based on performance.
Introduces three new curated datasets: FineMath, Stack-Edu, and SmolTalk.
Outperforms comparable small models including Qwen2.5-1.5B and Llama3.2-1B.
Demonstrates that careful data curation and mixing can push small-model performance well beyond compute-matched baselines.

papers.title: LIMO: Less is More for Reasoning
papers.abstract: Challenges the assumption that complex reasoning requires massive training data, showing sophisticated math reasoning emerges from a few hundred high-quality SFT examples, and proposes the Less-Is-More Reasoning Hypothesis.
findings: LIMO achieves 63.3% accuracy on AIME24 and 95.6% on MATH500 using only ~800 curated training samples (~1% of data used by prior approaches).
Shows a 45.8% absolute improvement on out-of-distribution benchmarks, outperforming models trained on 100x more data.
Proposes the Less-Is-More Reasoning Hypothesis: when domain knowledge is encoded in pretraining, reasoning emerges from minimal, strategically designed demonstrations.
Uses multi-layer filtering (difficulty, knowledge-point diversity, reasoning-chain quality) to build the compact dataset.
Demonstrates strong data-efficiency and generalization for SFT-based reasoning.

papers.title: Organize the Web: Constructing Domains Enhances Pre-Training Data Curation
papers.authors: Alexander Wettig, Kyle Lo, et al.
papers.abstract: Introduces WebOrganizer, which builds topic and format taxonomies for web pages and distills a large LLM classifier into small models to label documents, enabling domain-aware mixing as a complement to quality filtering.
findings: Develops two complementary domain taxonomies (topic and format), classifying web pages into 24 categories.
Scales labeling by distilling a Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct classifier into efficient 140M-parameter models.
Studies how to mix data from different domains to improve downstream tasks; combining effective topics and formats further boosts performance.
Constructing and mixing domains is a valuable complement to quality-based data curation.
Releases domain classifiers on HuggingFace and an interactive domain explorer.

papers.title: Scaling Test-Time Compute Without Verification or RL is Suboptimal
papers.abstract: Provides theory and experiments comparing verifier-free (distillation/cloning of search traces) versus verifier-based (RL, search against a verifier) methods for scaling test-time compute, showing the latter is provably better.
findings: Proves that verifier-based (VB) methods using RL or search against a verifier substantially outperform verifier-free (VF) approaches that distill/clone search traces, with the gap widening as test-time compute budget grows.
Shows a separation that scales with test-time budget, formalizing why verification matters for test-time scaling.
Empirically validates the gap on didactic and math reasoning settings (e.g., on a 3B/7B LLM), with VB outperforming VF by over 4x at large budgets in some settings.
Connects the advantage of verification to heterogeneity/anti-concentration of base policy correctness.
Argues compute should be invested in verifier-based RL rather than pure imitation when scaling inference.

papers.title: Data-Efficient Pretraining with Group-Level Data Influence Modeling (Group-MATES)
papers.abstract: Introduces Group-MATES, a method that optimizes pretraining data selection at the group level using a relational data influence model that captures relationships among training points, partitions data into clusters, and selects within clusters, evaluated under DataComp-LM setups.
findings: Achieves 3.5%-9.4% relative performance gains over random selection across 22 downstream tasks.
Nearly doubles the improvements achieved by state-of-the-art individual data selection baselines.
Reduces the number of tokens required to reach a given downstream performance by up to 1.75x.
Evaluated on DCLM 400M-4x, 1B-1x, and 3B-1x configurations using a relational (group-level) influence model.

papers.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
papers.abstract: Fully open-sources a state-of-the-art large-scale RL system (algorithm, code, dataset) for long-CoT reasoning. Introduces the Decoupled Clip and Dynamic Sampling Policy Optimization (DAPO) algorithm with four key techniques to stabilize and improve RL.
findings: DAPO achieves 50 points on AIME 2024 with Qwen2.5-32B base, outperforming DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B (47 points) while using 50% of the training steps.

Introduces four techniques: Clip-Higher (prevents entropy collapse, boosts diversity), Dynamic Sampling (efficiency/stability), Token-Level Policy Gradient Loss, and Overlong Reward Shaping (reduces reward noise).
Fully open-sources training code (built on the verl framework) and a curated dataset for reproducibility.
Token-level loss is shown to be critical in long-CoT scenarios where response lengths vary widely.
Clip-Higher mitigates entropy collapse, maintaining exploration over training.

papers.title: From 128K to 4M: Efficient Training of Ultra-Long Context Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Presents a systematic recipe combining efficient continued pretraining and instruction tuning to extend LLM context windows from 128K up to 4M tokens while preserving general capabilities.
findings: Extends context length from 128K to 1M, 2M, and 4M tokens via efficient continued pretraining plus instruction tuning.
UltraLong-8B (built on Llama3.1-Instruct) achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse long-context benchmarks.
Models maintain competitive performance on standard short-context benchmarks, showing balanced extension.
Provides in-depth analysis of scaling strategies and data composition for long-context training.
Establishes a reproducible framework for efficiently scaling context length while preserving capabilities.

papers.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
papers.abstract: Critically re-examines whether RLVR enables LLMs to acquire reasoning abilities beyond their base models by measuring pass@k at large k across model families and benchmarks.
findings: RLVR-trained models outperform base models at small k (e.g., k=1) but base models achieve higher pass@k when k is large, indicating RL narrows rather than expands the reasoning boundary.
RL improves sampling efficiency toward already-reachable correct paths but does not elicit fundamentally new reasoning patterns beyond the base model's support.
Findings hold across multiple model families and reasoning benchmarks.
Distillation, by contrast, can genuinely introduce new knowledge/patterns unlike RLVR.
Suggests current RLVR is bounded by the base model's capability distribution.

papers.title: The Leaderboard Illusion
papers.abstract: Identifies systematic distortions in Chatbot Arena rankings arising from undisclosed private testing, selective score disclosure, sampling disparities, and data access asymmetries between providers.
findings: Identifies 27 private LLM variants tested by Meta in the lead-up to the Llama-4 release
Google and OpenAI received an estimated 19.2% and 20.4% of all arena data, while 83 open-weight models combined received only an estimated 29.7%
Access to Chatbot Arena data can yield relative performance gains of up to 112% on the arena distribution, indicating overfitting risk

papers.title: Ultra-FineWeb: Efficient Data Filtering and Verification for High-Quality LLM Training Data
papers.abstract: Tackles data-quality challenges via an efficient verification strategy and optimized seed-data selection, using a lightweight fastText-based classifier to filter high-quality content from FineWeb. Produces Ultra-FineWeb (~1T English tokens and 120B Chinese tokens) while reducing experimental and inference costs and improving classifier robustness.
findings: Releases Ultra-FineWeb with approximately 1 trillion English tokens and 120 billion Chinese tokens.
Uses a lightweight fastText-based classifier rather than heavier model-based scoring to cut inference cost.
Introduces an efficient verification strategy plus optimized seed-data selection to improve filter robustness.
Reports that LLMs trained on Ultra-FineWeb show significant improvements across multiple benchmark tasks versus FineWeb baselines.

papers.title: AttentionInfluence: Adopting Attention Head Influence for Weak-to-Strong Pretraining Data Selection
papers.abstract: Proposes a training-free pretraining data selection method that masks attention heads in a small model to score reasoning-intensive data, enabling weak-to-strong selection where a small model selects data to improve a much larger model, applied to the SmolLM corpus.
findings: Uses a 1.3B-parameter dense model as a training-free data selector via attention-head masking.
Selects 73B tokens from the 241B-token SmolLM corpus.
Pretrains a 7B-parameter model on 1T tokens using the selected data.
Yields improvements ranging from 1.4pp to 3.5pp across MMLU, MMLU-Pro, AGIEval-en, GSM8K, and HumanEval.
Demonstrates weak-to-strong generalization: a small selector improves a much larger trained model.

papers.title: Qwen3 Technical Report
papers.abstract: Technical report for Qwen3, a family of dense and MoE LLMs (0.6B-235B) that unifies thinking and non-thinking modes in a single model with a controllable thinking budget, trained via a multi-stage pipeline.
findings: Integrates thinking mode (multi-step reasoning) and non-thinking mode (rapid responses) into one model with dynamic mode switching.
Introduces a thinking-budget mechanism letting users allocate inference compute adaptively by specifying a token budget.
Flagship models follow a four-stage training pipeline, the first two stages building thinking ability (long-CoT cold start + reasoning RL).
Spans dense and MoE architectures from 0.6B to 235B parameters.
Uses strong-to-weak distillation to transfer thinking/non-thinking behavior to smaller models, reducing compute versus per-model RL.

papers.title: LEXam: Benchmarking Legal Reasoning on 340 Law Exams
papers.abstract: A legal reasoning benchmark derived from real law school exams in English and German, covering open-ended and multiple-choice formats, with an ensemble LLM-judge approach validated by human legal experts.
findings: Comprises 7,537 law exam questions drawn from 340 law exams across 116 law school courses.
Spans both English and German, in open-ended and multiple-choice formats.
Finds current LLMs notably struggle with open questions requiring structured, multi-step legal reasoning.
Effectively differentiates models with varying capability levels.

papers.title: BizFinBench: A Business-Driven Real-World Financial Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs
papers.abstract: A real-world financial benchmark of annotated Chinese queries spanning five dimensions (numerical calculation, reasoning, information extraction, prediction recognition, knowledge QA), evaluated with an IteraJudge protocol to reduce evaluator bias.
findings: Comprises 6,781 annotated queries across 9 fine-grained categories within 5 dimensions.
Evaluates 25 proprietary and open-source models; no model dominates across all tasks.
Numerical Calculation top scores: DeepSeek-R1 64.04, Claude-3.5-Sonnet 63.18; Reasoning: ChatGPT-o3 83.58, Gemini-2.0-Flash 81.15.
LLMs handle routine financial queries adequately but struggle with complex reasoning scenarios.

papers.title: Toward Scientific Reasoning in LLMs: Training from Expert Discussions via Reinforcement Learning (Genome-Bench)
papers.abstract: An end-to-end pipeline that converts over a decade of genome-engineering expert forum discussions into an RL-friendly multiple-choice benchmark (Genome-Bench), then fine-tunes LLMs with rule-based rewards to improve domain-specific scientific reasoning.
findings: Builds Genome-Bench with over 3,000 high-quality QA pairs from real-world expert discussions.
RL from scientific discussions improves model performance by more than 15% over the base model on Genome-Bench.
Fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B reaches performance comparable to leading models such as DeepSeek-R1.
Described as the first end-to-end pipeline for teaching LLMs to reason from scientific discussions, with potential to generalize beyond biology.

papers.title: SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents
papers.abstract: An automated pipeline that continuously extracts real-world interactive software engineering tasks from GitHub repositories, producing both a large-scale RL training dataset and a continuously refreshed, contamination-free evaluation benchmark for SWE agents.
findings: Releases a public dataset of over 21,000 interactive Python-based SWE tasks suitable for RL of agents at scale.
Provides a continuously refreshed, contamination-free benchmark built from fresh GitHub tasks.
Comparison against SWE-bench Verified shows performance of some language models may be inflated due to data contamination.
Targets the twin problems of scarce real-environment training data and rapid benchmark obsolescence.

papers.title: The Entropy Mechanism of Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Language Models
papers.abstract: Studies the entropy collapse problem that limits scaling RL for reasoning LLMs, providing theoretical analysis of entropy dynamics and proposing techniques to maintain exploration.
findings: Identifies that tokens with strong positive covariance between probability and advantage primarily drive entropy collapse during RL.
Proposes Clip-Cov and KL-Cov, which clip or apply a KL penalty to high-covariance tokens to restrict their updates and preserve entropy.
These methods help the policy escape entropy collapse and achieve better downstream performance, enabling more sustained RL scaling.
Provides a predictable relationship (entropy-performance exchange) where policy entropy decays as performance rises, bottlenecking improvement.
Maintaining exploration directly translates into higher final reasoning accuracy.

papers.title: ProRL: Prolonged Reinforcement Learning Expands Reasoning Boundaries in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Introduces ProRL, a prolonged RL training methodology with KL divergence control, reference policy resetting, and a diverse task suite, arguing that with enough training RL can expand reasoning boundaries beyond the base model.
findings: RL-trained models consistently outperform base models across pass@k evaluations, including cases where base models fail entirely regardless of number of attempts.
Prolonged RL uncovers novel reasoning strategies inaccessible to base models even under extensive sampling, contrasting with the pass@k narrowing claim.
Reasoning boundary improvements correlate strongly with base-model task competence and training duration.
Uses KL divergence control and reference policy resetting to enable stable, long-duration RL training.
Releases the Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B model weights.

papers.title: OpenThoughts: Data Recipes for Reasoning Models
papers.abstract: A systematic study of data-curation recipes for distilling reasoning into models via SFT, culminating in the OpenThoughts3-1.2M dataset and the OpenThinker3-7B model.
findings: OpenThinker3-7B (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct fine-tuned on OpenThoughts3-1.2M) is state-of-the-art among open-data models at the 7B scale.
Outperforms the DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B model by 12.4 points on average across 12 reasoning benchmarks.
Scales the Sky-T1/OpenThoughts pipeline with augmented question diversity and synthetic question generation strategies.
Conducts over a thousand controlled experiments to identify effective data-curation choices (question sourcing, filtering, teacher selection).
Demonstrates that careful SFT distillation data design rivals or beats RL-trained reasoning at small scale.

papers.title: The Common Pile v0.1: An 8TB Dataset of Public Domain and Openly Licensed Text
papers.abstract: Addresses concerns about unlicensed text in LLM training by collecting, curating, and releasing an 8TB collection of openly licensed and public-domain text drawn from 30 diverse sources spanning research papers, code, books, encyclopedias, educational materials, and audio transcripts. The dataset is validated by training two 7B-parameter LLMs (Comma v0.1-1T and 2T) that attain competitive performance to models trained on unlicensed text under similar compute budgets.
findings: Largest collection of openly licensed text to date: an 8TB dataset drawn from 30 sources across diverse domains.
Trained two 7B-parameter models: Comma v0.1-1T (1 trillion tokens) and Comma v0.1-2T (2 trillion tokens).
Both models attain competitive performance with LLMs trained on unlicensed text at similar compute budgets, such as Llama 1 and Llama 2 7B.
Demonstrates that openly licensed data alone can be sufficient for competitive pretraining, challenging the assumption that unlicensed web text is required.

papers.title: tau2-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment
papers.abstract: A benchmark that models customer-service agent interaction as a Dec-POMDP where both the agent and the user can take tool actions in a shared environment, with a compositional task generator, reliable user simulator, and a new telecom domain.
findings: Introduces dual-control (Dec-POMDP) evaluation where both agent and user use tools, unlike prior single-control benchmarks.
Adds a telecom domain with a compositional task generator producing diverse, verifiable tasks from atomic components.
Reports significant agent performance drops when shifting from no-user to dual-control settings.
Separates reasoning errors from coordination failures via a reliable user simulator.

papers.title: Magistral
papers.abstract: Technical report for Magistral, Mistral's first reasoning model, built with a from-scratch scalable RL pipeline relying solely on their own models and infrastructure rather than distilled traces from prior models.
findings: Ground-up RL approach: avoids RL traces distilled from existing reasoning models, relying solely on Mistral's own models and infrastructure.
Presents a simple method to force the reasoning language of the model.
Shows RL on text-only data maintains or improves multimodal understanding, instruction following, and function calling.
Magistral Medium is trained on Mistral Medium 3 with pure RL; Magistral Small (Apache 2.0) adds cold-start data distilled from Magistral Medium.
Demonstrates that pure RL training can reach strong reasoning while preserving most of the initial checkpoint's capabilities.

papers.title: Spurious Rewards: Rethinking Training Signals in RLVR
papers.abstract: Shows that RLVR can elicit strong math reasoning in Qwen2.5-Math even with spurious rewards (random, format-only, or incorrect labels), raising questions about what RLVR actually optimizes and how model-dependent the effect is.
findings: On Qwen2.5-Math-7B, RLVR improves MATH-500 by 21.4% (random reward), 13.8% (format reward), 24.1% (incorrect label), 26.0% (1-shot RL), 27.1% (majority voting), vs 29.1% with ground-truth rewards.
Spurious rewards that work for Qwen often fail to help other model families like Llama3 or OLMo2.
'Code reasoning' (thinking in code without execution) becomes a distinctive Qwen2.5-Math behavior, rising from 65% to over 90% after RLVR even with spurious rewards.

edges.note: RLVR gains may be elicitation, not teaching

papers.title: Agent-RLVR: Training Software Engineering Agents via Guidance and Environment Rewards
papers.abstract: Extends Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) to complex agentic SWE settings by adding agent guidance that actively steers the agent toward successful trajectories, combined with environment validation rewards.
findings: On SWE-Bench Verified, Qwen-2.5-72B-Instruct improves from 9.4% pass@1 (baseline) to 22.4% pass@1 with Agent-RLVR.
Adding test-time reward model training raises performance further to 27.8% pass@1.
Guidance mechanism provides informational cues that help agents recover from high-failure-rate trajectories.
Demonstrates RLVR can be made effective in multi-step agentic environments where vanilla RLVR degrades.

papers.title: RoboArena: Distributed Real-World Evaluation of Generalist Robot Policies
papers.abstract: A distributed, crowd-sourced methodology for evaluating generalist robot policies via double-blind pairwise comparisons across multiple institutions, aggregating preference feedback into reliable performance rankings.
findings: Conducts over 600 pairwise real-robot evaluations across diverse settings.
Tests 7 generalist policies across 7 academic institutions on the DROID platform.
Uses double-blind pairwise preference feedback rather than centralized standardized tasks.
Produces more accurate, scalable, and resilient rankings than conventional centralized evaluation.

papers.title: RefineX: Learning to Refine Pre-training Data at Scale from Expert-Guided Programs
papers.abstract: Proposes RefineX, a framework for large-scale refinement of pretraining data through programmatic editing. It distills expert-guided refinement results into edit-based deletion programs to train an efficient model that systematically improves corpus instances while preserving text diversity and naturalness.
findings: On the 750M model, RefineX yields 2.6%-7.2% average gains on lighteval tasks.
Achieves comparable performance using significantly fewer training tokens.
Outperforms models trained on raw, filtered, or alternatively refined data across diverse downstream tasks.
Beats prior approaches such as end-to-end generation and Prox-C.
Distills expert-guided refinement into edit-based deletion programs to preserve diversity and naturalness.

papers.title: Training Long-Context, Multi-Turn Software Engineering Agents with Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Applies modified DAPO-style RL to train long-context, multi-turn LLM agents for real-world software engineering tasks (issue resolution) without SFT, in interactive tool-using environments.
findings: Trains a multi-turn SWE agent with RL (a modified DAPO algorithm) directly, without an SFT warm-up stage.
On SWE-bench Verified, raises a Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct-based agent's resolve rate from 11% to 39% using RL alone.
Handles long-context, multi-turn interaction with a real code repository environment and tool use (editing, testing).
Demonstrates that purely RL-trained agents are competitive with much larger or SFT-pipelined open-weight agents on SWE tasks.
Addresses practical challenges of long-horizon, multi-turn credit assignment in agentic RL.

papers.title: BeyondWeb: Lessons from Scaling Synthetic Data for Trillion-scale Pretraining
papers.abstract: Introduces BeyondWeb, a synthetic data generation framework using targeted document rephrasing to produce diverse, relevant, information-dense synthetic pretraining data, addressing diminishing returns from simply scaling web-data quantity at trillion-token scale.
findings: Outperforms Cosmopedia by up to 5.1 percentage points and Nemotron-Synth by up to 2.6pp across 14 benchmarks.
Delivers up to 7.7x faster training than open web data and 2.7x faster than Nemotron-Synth.
A 3B model trained for 180B tokens on BeyondWeb outperforms an 8B model trained for the same token budget on Cosmopedia.
Emphasizes that best outcomes require jointly optimizing many factors rather than a single solution.
Trains 1B, 3B, and 8B models to validate scaling of synthetic data to trillion-token regimes.

papers.title: Nemotron-CC-Math: A 133 Billion-Token-Scale High Quality Math Pretraining Dataset
papers.abstract: Builds a high-quality math pretraining corpus from Common Crawl using layout-aware rendering with lynx plus a targeted LLM-based cleaning stage that recovers equations in MathJax, KaTeX, and MathML formats, preserving structure and standardizing notation to LaTeX. Releases Nemotron-CC-Math-3+ (133B tokens) and Nemotron-CC-Math-4+ (52B tokens).
findings: Nemotron-CC-Math-4+ (52B tokens) contains 5.5 times more tokens than FineMath-4+ and surpasses prior open math datasets including MegaMath, FineMath, and OpenWebMath.
Pretraining an 8B model yields +4.8 to +12.6 gains on MATH over strong baselines.
Yields +4.6 to +14.3 gains on MBPP+ over strong baselines.
Improves general reasoning on both MMLU and MMLU-Stem.
Uses layout-aware lynx rendering plus targeted LLM cleaning to recover equations across MathJax, KaTeX, and MathML and standardize to LaTeX.

papers.title: Knowledge Collapse in LLMs: When Fluency Survives but Facts Fail under Recursive Synthetic Training
papers.abstract: Examines how recursive training on synthetic data causes knowledge collapse, a distinct three-stage phenomenon where factual accuracy deteriorates while surface fluency persists, producing confidently-wrong outputs, and distinguishes this instruction-following/knowledge collapse from traditional distributional model collapse.
findings: Defines knowledge collapse as a three-stage phenomenon: factual accuracy deteriorates while surface fluency persists, creating confidently-wrong outputs.
Distinguishes knowledge/instruction-following collapse from traditional distributional model collapse.
Shows recursive synthetic training degrades facts faster than it degrades fluency.
Proposes domain-specific synthetic training as a mitigation strategy.

papers.title: AgentArch: A Comprehensive Benchmark to Evaluate Agent Architectures in Enterprise
papers.abstract: An enterprise-focused benchmark that systematically evaluates combinations of agent design dimensions (orchestration strategy, ReAct vs function calling, memory architecture, thinking-tool integration) across state-of-the-art LLMs.
findings: Evaluates 18 distinct agentic configurations across state-of-the-art LLMs over 4 critical design dimensions.
Reports maximum success rates of only 35.3% on complex tasks and 70.8% on simpler tasks.
Finds model-specific architectural preferences, challenging one-size-fits-all agent designs.
Highlights limited empirical understanding of how design dimensions interact in enterprise multi-agent systems.

papers.title: FinSearchComp: Towards a Realistic, Expert-Level Evaluation of Financial Search and Reasoning
papers.abstract: The first fully open-source agent benchmark for realistic, open-domain financial search and reasoning, with three task types mirroring analyst workflows and expert-annotated, multi-stage quality assurance.
findings: Contains 635 questions spanning global and Greater China markets across three tasks: Time-Sensitive Data Fetching, Simple Historical Lookup, and Complex Historical Investigation.
Engages 70 professional financial experts for annotation and QA; evaluates 21 models/products.
Grok 4 (web) tops the global subset approaching expert-level accuracy; DouBao (web) leads the Greater China subset.
Web search and financial plugins substantially improve results; model origin and tool selection significantly impact performance.

papers.title: Synthetic Bootstrapped Pretraining
papers.abstract: Proposes a pretraining procedure that first learns a model of relations between documents and then uses it to synthesize a vast new corpus for joint training, capturing inter-document correlations that standard token-level next-token prediction within single documents misses.
findings: Evaluated on 3B- and 6B-parameter models trained on up to 1T tokens from scratch in a compute-matched setup.
Delivers up to 60% of the performance improvement attainable by an oracle upper bound that has access to 20x more unique data.
Synthesized documents go beyond mere paraphrases, representing conceptual abstraction rather than surface rewriting.
Targets the data wall by extracting more signal from a fixed unique-data budget via inter-document relations.

papers.title: Fleming-R1: Toward Expert-Level Medical Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: A medical reasoning model targeting verifiable clinical reasoning via a reasoning-oriented data strategy combining curated datasets with knowledge-graph synthesis, chain-of-thought cold start, and a two-stage RL framework using Group Relative Policy Optimization.
findings: The 7B variant surpasses significantly larger baselines on medical benchmarks.
The 32B model achieves near-parity with GPT-4o and consistently outperforms strong open-source alternatives.
Uses knowledge-graph-guided data synthesis to target identified reasoning failure modes.
Released publicly to support transparent, reproducible, auditable medical AI.

papers.title: SWE-Bench Pro: Can AI Agents Solve Long-Horizon Software Engineering Tasks?
papers.abstract: A contamination-resistant, human-verified benchmark of long-horizon software engineering tasks drawn from actively maintained repositories, spanning business applications, B2B services, and developer tools. Tasks often require patches across multiple files and substantial code modifications taking professional engineers hours to days.
findings: Contains 1,865 problems sourced from 41 actively maintained repositories.
Repositories split across a public set (11 repos), a held-out set (12 repos), and a commercial set of 18 proprietary repos.
Tasks are long-horizon, frequently requiring multi-file patches and substantial code changes.
All tasks go through a human augmentation and verification process to ensure descriptions and tests are well specified.

papers.title: The Data-Quality Illusion: Rethinking Classifier-based Quality Filtering for LLM Pretraining (Removing Noise, not Finding Gold)
papers.abstract: Analyzes Classifier-based Quality Filtering (CQF), the dominant method for filtering web-crawled pretraining data. Shows that training on CQF-selected data can outperform training directly on the high-quality target set, explaining this via the observation that CQF implicitly filters both the high- and low-quality datasets, and proposes an optimization-driven notion of data quality estimable through small-scale proxy experiments.
findings: Training on CQF-selected data can outperform training directly on the high-quality set, even when that set is sufficiently large.
CQF improves downstream task performance but does not necessarily improve language modeling on the high-quality dataset itself.
Explains the effect by showing CQF implicitly filters the high-quality dataset as well, acting more like noise removal than gold finding.
Proposes an optimization-driven notion of data quality reliably estimated via small-scale proxy experiments.

papers.title: Demystifying Synthetic Data in LLM Pre-training: A Systematic Study of Scaling Laws, Benefits, and Pitfalls
papers.abstract: A large-scale empirical study comparing natural web data against synthetic approaches (rephrased text and generated textbooks) for LLM pretraining, analyzing impact on performance, scaling, and compute efficiency across model sizes and data budgets.
findings: Pretraining on 1/3 rephrased synthetic data mixed with 2/3 natural web text can speed up reaching equivalent validation loss by 5-10x at larger data budgets.
Good ratios of synthetic data empirically converge to ~30% for rephrased synthetic data across model sizes and budgets.
Larger generator models do not necessarily yield better pretraining data than ~8B-parameter models.
Textbook-style synthetic data leads to notably higher loss on many downstream domains, especially at small data budgets.
Study spans over 1000 LLMs and over 100k GPU hours.

papers.title: X-VLA: Soft-Prompted Transformer as Scalable Cross-Embodiment Vision-Language-Action Model
papers.abstract: A scalable cross-embodiment vision-language-action model that uses learnable per-data-source soft-prompt embeddings with a flow-matching-based Transformer to handle heterogeneous robot data across embodiments, environments, and tasks.
findings: Introduces soft prompts (learnable embeddings per data source) with minimally added parameters to absorb cross-embodiment data heterogeneity.
X-VLA-0.9B simultaneously achieves SOTA performance across a sweep of benchmarks.
Validated across 6 simulations and 3 real-world robots.
Demonstrates flexible dexterity and quick adaptation across embodiments, environments, and tasks.

papers.title: Escaping Model Collapse via Synthetic Data Verification: Near-term Improvements and Long-term Convergence
papers.abstract: Investigates how to prevent model collapse from iteratively retraining generative models on self-generated synthetic data, showing both theoretically and empirically that incorporating external verification (human or from a superior model) prevents collapse, with verifier-guided retraining converging to the verifier's knowledge center.
findings: Shows incorporating external verification (human or a superior model) prevents model collapse in self-consuming training loops.
Theoretical analysis in linear regression: verifier-guided retraining produces initial gains but eventually converges to the verifier's knowledge center.
Validated across linear regression, VAEs on MNIST, and fine-tuning SmolLM2-135M on XSUM.
Frames verification as the key mechanism distinguishing safe self-improvement loops from degenerative ones.

papers.title: Chem-R: Learning to Reason as a Chemist
papers.abstract: A chemical reasoning model built via a three-phase framework (foundation training, protocol distillation with expert reasoning traces, and multi-task optimization) to emulate expert chemist reasoning across molecular and reaction tasks.
findings: Surpasses Gemini-2.5-Pro and DeepSeek-R1 by up to 32% on molecular tasks.
Outperforms leading models by up to 48% on reaction tasks.
Consistently exceeds existing chemical foundation models across molecular- and reaction-level benchmarks.
Uses distilled expert reasoning traces (protocol distillation) to instill structured chemical reasoning.

papers.title: P1: Mastering Physics Olympiads with Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: A family of open-source LLMs trained purely via reinforcement learning for Olympiad-level physics reasoning, achieving gold-medal performance at the International Physics Olympiad and strong cross-domain generalization.
findings: P1-235B-A22B (235B total / 22B active) is the first open-source model with Gold-medal performance at IPhO 2025.
Won 12 gold medals across 13 international/regional physics competitions in 2024/2025.
P1-30B-A3B (30B / 3B active) reaches silver-medal performance on IPhO 2025, surpassing most open-source models.
P1-235B-A22B combined with the PhysicsMinions agent framework achieves overall No.1 on IPhO 2025; models also generalize to math and coding.

papers.title: SkyRL-Agent: Efficient RL Training for Multi-turn LLM Agent
papers.abstract: A framework for efficient multi-turn LLM agent RL training featuring asynchronous dispatching, lightweight tool integration, and flexible backend interoperability, used to train a 32B SWE agent that generalizes across agentic tasks.
findings: Trains SA-SWE-32B (from Qwen3-32B), improving SWE-Bench Verified from 24.4% to 39.4% Pass@1.
Achieves over 2x cost reduction versus prior similar-performing models.
Pipeline dispatcher yields a 1.55x speedup over naive asynchronous batching.
SWE-only training generalizes to Terminal-Bench, BrowseComp-Plus, and WebArena.

papers.title: Thinking While Speaking: Inference-Time Knowledge Transfer for Responsive and Intelligent Conversational Voice Agents
papers.abstract: Voice agents face a fundamental tension: the reasoning, retrieval, and tool use that make foundation models capable are iterative and slow, while conversational interaction demands responses on a millisecond timescale. Smaller, real-time models meet the latency bar but cannot match foundation models on complex tasks, leaving current voice agents to trade away either responsiveness or capability. We introduce conversational infill, where a small talker model both immediately generates contextually grounded responses to hide the latency of an external reasoner model and fluently integrates streamed reasoner knowledge into its responses during inference. We curate a 290,571-example synthetic dataset spanning six domains and demonstrate that this task is learnable across seven widely used small language models ranging from 135M to 1.7B parameters. Our system implementation, ConvFill, sustains millisecond-level time-to-first-response while closing the accuracy gap to within 6.3% of the corresponding frontier reasoner performance. In a live user study (n=18) with talker deployments running on an Apple M2 SoC, participants rank ConvFill on par with frontier models overall, prefer it for retrieval-heavy tasks, and rate it significantly more responsive. These results show that conversational infill unlocks a new point on the latency-capability Pareto frontier, offering a practical path toward voice agents that are both responsive and highly capable. Code, models, and datasets are available at https://github.com/vysri/conversational-infill.
findings: Our system implementation, ConvFill, sustains millisecond-level time-to-first-response while closing the accuracy gap to within 6.3% of the corresponding frontier reasoner performance.

papers.title: Qwen-RobotManip Technical Report: Alignment Unlocks Scale for Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Foundation models in language and multimodality achieve strong generalization by aligning heterogeneous data under a unified formulation and training at scale. In this report, we investigate whether this scaling recipe can be applied to robotic manipulation to achieve genuine generalization. This is challenging because, unlike text, manipulation data is heterogeneous by nature, expensive to collect, and narrow in diversity, making alignment and scale simultaneously difficult. We present Qwen-RobotManip, a generalizable Vision-Language-Action foundation model built on Qwen-VL. Qwen-RobotManip introduces a unified alignment framework across the representation, motion, and behavioral dimensions of manipulation, making large-scale multi-source training coherent rather than conflicting. This alignment capability in turn enables Qwen-RobotManip to absorb manipulation data at a scale that prior training regimes could not sustain. A human-to-robot synthesis pipeline converts egocentric hand demonstrations into robot trajectories across 15 platforms, and a rigorous curation pipeline harmonizes heterogeneous datasets. Using only open-source datasets and human videos without proprietary data collection, Qwen-RobotManip constructs a ~38,100-hour pretraining corpus and exhibits emergent generalization capabilities, including zero-shot instruction following, robustness to perturbations, reactive error recovery, and cross-embodiment transfer. We find that standard benchmarks fail to capture pretraining quality and instead adopt OOD settings including RoboCasa365, LIBERO-Plus, EBench, RoboTwin-Clean2Rand, RoboTwin-IF, and RoboTwin-XE. Qwen-RobotManip substantially outperforms prior state-of-the-art models, including π0.5, across all OOD settings, ranks 1st in RoboChallenge with a 20% relative improvement, and is validated on real-robot platforms including AgileX ALOHA, Franka, UR, and ARX.
findings: Foundation models in language and multimodality achieve strong generalization by aligning heterogeneous data under a unified formulation and training at scale.

papers.title: Qwen-RobotNav Technical Report: A Scalable Navigation Model Designed for an Agentic Navigation System
papers.abstract: Agentic navigation systems require a base navigation model whose observation strategy can be externally reconfigured at inference time, because instruction following, object search, target tracking, and autonomous driving share the same perception-planning backbone yet demand fundamentally different strategies for consuming the visual stream. We present Qwen-RobotNav, a scalable navigation model built on Qwen-RobotNav that addresses it through a parameterised interface with two complementary dimensions: multiple task modes that select the navigation behaviour, and controllable observation parameters (e.g., token budget, per-camera weights) that govern how visual history is encoded. With training-time randomization over all parameters, Qwen-RobotNav is robust to any inference-time configuration requiring zero architectural modification to the Qwen-RobotNav backbone. We train Qwen-RobotNav on 15.6M samples; co-training with vision-language data prevents the collapse into reactive action-sequence mappers observed in trajectory-only training. The parameterised interface also makes Qwen-RobotNav a natural building block for agentic systems: for long-horizon scenarios, an upper-level planner decomposes goals into sub-tasks and dynamically switches Qwen-RobotNav's task mode and context strategy mid-episode, composing complex behaviours from repeated calls to the same model. Extensive experiments show that Qwen-RobotNav sets new state-of-the-art results across major navigation benchmarks. The model exhibits favourable scaling from 2B to 8B parameters, with joint multi-task training developing a shared spatial-planning substrate that transfers across task families, and demonstrates strong zero-shot generalisation to real-world robots across diverse environments.
findings: Extensive experiments show that Qwen-RobotNav sets new state-of-the-art results across major navigation benchmarks.

papers.title: AgentOdyssey: Open-Ended Long-Horizon Text Game Generation for Test-Time Continual Learning Agents
papers.abstract: For agents to learn continuously from interaction with the world at test time, they must be able to explore effectively, acquire new world knowledge and skills, retain relevant episodic experiences, and plan over long horizons. To evaluate these key abilities of test-time continual learning agents, we introduce AgentOdyssey, a novel evaluation framework that procedurally generates open-ended text games with rich entities, world dynamics, and long-horizon tasks. Critically, AgentOdyssey goes beyond the conventional machine learning assumption that learning does not occur at test time by placing agents in a continuous, long-horizon setting that interleaves learning and inference throughout deployment. We further propose a multifaceted evaluation methodology that measures not only game progress but also offers diagnostic tests on world knowledge acquisition, episodic memory, object and action exploration, action diversity, and model cost. We evaluate diverse agent paradigms in the generated games. Our experimental results reveal critical limits in agents' key abilities, as well as factors that influence their meaningful horizon. Although performance scales with stronger base models, even the top agent remains far below human performance, leaving substantial headroom for improvement. Among agent mechanisms, we find that short-term memory benefits multiple agent paradigms and is an important component of agent test-time training.
findings: Although performance scales with stronger base models, even the top agent remains far below human performance, leaving substantial headroom for improvement.

papers.title: The Galaxy's Guide to the Tokenizer: A Benchmark for Scientific Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Tokenization is central to adapting scientific data for transformer-based foundation models, yet its impact on learned representations remains poorly understood. We compare four tokenization strategies, Affine, AIM, JetFormer, and VQ-VAE, within a unified transformer framework for astronomical imaging. Using 640,000 galaxy images from the DESI Legacy Survey and a shared AstroPT backbone, we evaluate each method on reconstruction fidelity and prediction of physical properties. Our results reveal trade-offs across approaches. The flow-based JetFormer achieves higher reconstruction quality, while VQ-VAE yields strong probe performance for galaxy physical properties. Affine and AIM better preserve localized morphological information. We find that reconstruction and representation quality are decoupled, and no single method consistently performs best across the tasks considered here. By grounding our evaluation in independently measured physical quantities, we hope this study serves to highlight the potential of scientific data as a basis for constructing interpretable benchmarks for foundation models.
findings: The flow-based JetFormer achieves higher reconstruction quality, while VQ-VAE yields strong probe performance for galaxy physical properties.

By grounding our evaluation in independently measured physical quantities, we hope this study serves to highlight the potential of scientific data as a basis for constructing interpretable benchmarks for foundation models.

papers.title: The Tatoxa System for Text Detoxification in Low-Resource Languages: The Case of Tatar
papers.abstract: Text detoxification, the automated detection and mitigation of abusive and harmful content, is essential for ensuring the safety of online communities and protecting users. However, low resource languages such as Tatar have received little research attention. In this paper we present Tatoxa, a novel state-of-the-art system for text detoxification in the Tatar language. Comparative experiments show that the proposed approach outperforms existing open source and proprietary commercial LLMs on key quality metrics. We also introduce a new dataset for text detoxification in Tatar, designed for fine tuning and evaluation in low resource settings. Finally, cross lingual transfer experiments indicate that transfer from other languages, including the culturally close Russian, performs significantly worse than training on native Tatar data even when a large Russian corpus is available.
findings: In this paper we present Tatoxa, a novel state-of-the-art system for text detoxification in the Tatar language.
Comparative experiments show that the proposed approach outperforms existing open source and proprietary commercial LLMs on key quality metrics.

papers.title: To Run or Not to Run: Analyzing the Cost-Effectiveness of Code Execution in LLM-Based Program Repair
papers.abstract: LLM-based agents for program repair are increasingly built on a "generate-run-revise" paradigm, iteratively executing tests to evaluate and refine patches. This execution-based approach has become standard practice in state-of-the-art systems. However, executions can be time-consuming and expensive, yet their impact on these agents remains underexplored. In this paper, we conduct a two-stage empirical study over execution behavior in LLM-based program repair. To characterize execution behavior at scale, we first analyze 7,745 agent traces from SWE-bench leaderboard submissions. Second, we evaluate 3,000 end-to-end repair attempts across 200 SWE-bench instances and three agents (Claude Code, Codex, and the open-source OpenCode) under four execution paradigms, which allows for a fine-grained comparison of performance and cost. Our analysis reveals three key observations: (1) Code execution is used across all agents and models analyzed, with an average of 8.8 test runs per task. Execution behavior varies substantially across agents and models, with frequency ranging from 2 to 19 per task, and late-stage executions consistently achieve higher success rates than early-stage ones. (2) Execution restrictions have little effect on repair success: on commercial agents with SOTA models the resolve-rate gap between Prohibited and Unrestricted is only 1.25 percentage points and not statistically significant, while Prohibited saves substantial token and wall-clock cost. (3) Execution benefit is concentrated rather than uniform. These patterns suggest that current agents apply execution indiscriminately, paying its cost on instances where it provides little benefit. Execution, therefore, should be treated as a resource with an explicit cost-benefit tradeoff, not a default capability.
findings: This execution-based approach has become standard practice in state-of-the-art systems.

Execution behavior varies substantially across agents and models, with frequency ranging from 2 to 19 per task, and late-stage executions consistently achieve higher success rates than early-stage ones.
